intro: Čara, a village on Korčula about 25 kilometres by road from Korčula town, is dominated, in the Croatian tourist board's words, by its parish church of St Peter and a century-old cypress the villagers are proud of. The cypress has been on Croatia's register of protected natural monuments since 1948. Its age is a puzzle: the tourist board says a century, other tourism pages say 500 years, and nobody has measured it.
meta_description: The cypress of Čara on Korčula: a protected tree beside the parish church of St Peter, a century to 500 years old depending on the source.
question_meta: Čara's old cypress stands by the parish church of St Peter on Korčula; its age is put anywhere from a century to 500 years.
question_answer: The cypress of Čara stands beside the parish church of St Peter in the centre of the village, on Korčula, and has been a protected natural monument since 1948. The tourist board calls it century-old; other pages say 500 years, and none of these ages comes from a measurement.
question_context: Very little has been written about the Čara cypress, and what has been written disagrees. Croatia's tourist board says the village is dominated by the parish church of St Peter and a century-old cypress that locals are particularly proud of. Other tourism pages put the tree at 500 years. The gap between the two figures is four centuries, and neither is based on a measured date, so it is best read as an old cypress of unknown age. It is one tree, entered on the national register of protected natural monuments in 1948. The church beside it dates from the 15th or 16th century, depending on the source, and holds an altarpiece attributed to Bassano. Čara lies about 25 kilometres west of Korčula town by road, roughly 30 to 40 minutes by car, and island buses are infrequent, so it is a drive and a stop. Our pin is the register's point in the village centre rather than a fix on the trunk, and nobody has published its height or girth.

trees.story:
Čara, says Croatia's tourist board, is dominated by two things, the parish church of St Peter and a century-old cypress that the villagers are particularly proud of. That one sentence is most of what anyone has put in writing about the tree.

How old it is depends on who is talking. The tourist board says a century. Other tourism pages say 500 years. Neither figure comes from a measurement, and the gap between them is four centuries, so read every number you meet for this tree as a guess. What is firm is that it is old enough to have been entered on Croatia's register of protected natural monuments in 1948, as the cypress of Čara, a single tree.

The church beside it dates from the 15th or 16th century, depending on the source, and holds an altarpiece attributed to Bassano. Village, church and cypress sit on the island of Korčula, about 25 kilometres by road from Korčula town, so this is a drive and a stop rather than a walk from the old town.

Our pin is the register's own point in the village centre, not a fix on the trunk. Nobody has published its height or girth either. If you stop in Čara, a photograph and a sense of its size would tell us more than the tourism pages have.

trees.verify_notes: Register point 42.935398,16.93436 falls in Čara village (OSM reverse geocode: road 6268, Čara). It is the register's own point, not a GPS fix at the trunk, and the church position was not confirmed in OSM, so approximate with a small named site. Croatian Tourist Board (visit-croatia.hr) page for Čara: the village is dominated by the parish Church of St. Peter and the century-old cypress that locals are particularly proud of (only 'century-old'; page undated, so alive is by present tense only; flagged). Other tourism pages claim 500 years; a university thesis on Korčula's vegetation reportedly lists a cypress of about 450 years in Čara among the island's park-architecture monuments (seen only in a search summary, host repozitorij.unizd.hr returns 418 to automation, not recorded as fact). Ages conflict (100+ / 450 / 500): keep broad, none sourced to a measurement. No girth or height found. Register date 1948-11-12 is from our extract. Church of St Peter is 15th to 16th century (sources disagree); altarpiece attributed to Bassano.
